claims.claim: Copy job modes, watermark column types, strictly larger watermark rule, CDC captures deletes, watermark cannot detect deletes, reset to full copy per job or table.
Update methods Append (default), Merge (primary key by default), Overwrite and SCD Type 2.
CDC replication in Copy job is in preview.

concept_html:
A Copy job copies data in one of two modes. Full copy moves everything on every run. Incremental copy moves everything on the first run, then only new or changed data. The job tracks the state of the last successful run itself (Microsoft Learn, checked September 2026).

Incremental copy works in one of two ways:

  • Watermark. You pick an incremental column, such as a ROWVERSION, a datetime, a date or an increasing integer. Each subsequent load copies rows whose value is larger than any value copied before.
  • CDC (preview in Copy job). If change data capture is enabled on the source database, the job reads its change stream and copies every insert, update and delete since the last run. You do not choose a column.

The watermark method has two blind spots, and both follow from "larger than":

  • It cannot see deletes. A deleted row simply stops appearing, and the destination keeps it.
  • It misses late rows. A row committed after the run, with a watermark value at or below the one already copied, is never picked up. A modified_at set by the application clock, or several rows written in the same second, causes this.

Prefer CDC when you need deletes, or a ROWVERSION column, which the database increments on every change. Microsoft also lets you reset incremental copy to a full copy, for the whole job or per table, to recover.

Choose the update method for the destination on purpose. The default is Append, which keeps full history, and appends every changed row again as a new row. Merge updates existing rows by key (the primary key by default), Overwrite replaces the data, and SCD Type 2 keeps versioned history. For a silver table that must hold one row per key, choose Merge.

exercises.solution:
Row = dict[str, int]


def next_batch(rows: list[Row], last_wm: int | None) -> tuple[list[Row], int | None]:
    """Rows above the watermark, and the new watermark.

    Args:
        rows: Source rows, each with an integer rv.
        last_wm: Largest rv copied so far, or None before the first run.

    Returns:
        The rows to copy and the watermark to store.
    """
    batch = [r for r in rows if last_wm is None or r["rv"] > last_wm]
    if not batch:
        return [], last_wm
    return batch, max(r["rv"] for r in batch)

title: Incremental copy with a watermark, or with CDC
why_html: An order table was copied incrementally on modified_at, set by the ordering app. At 23:59:59 one batch committed after the nightly run had read up to 23:59:59. Those rows carried the same timestamp as the last copied row, so they were never picked up. Finance found 212 missing orders at month end. CDC, or a ROWVERSION column, would have caught them.
